subject: gk
question: The terms, ‘Aus’, ‘Aman’ and ‘Boro’, are associated with which crop in West Bengal?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rice**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Rice** is the staple food of West Bengal and is grown extensively across the region.
 
• The terms 'Aus', 'Aman', and 'Boro' refer to different **rice cultivation seasons** in West Bengal.
 
• 'Aus' rice is typically sown in the months of **March to April** and harvested in **June to July**.
 
• 'Aman' rice is sown during the **monsoon season** (June to July) and harvested in **November to December**, while 'Boro' rice is grown in the winter season and harvested in the **spring** (February to May).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aus**

 
 
• Aus is an early season variety of rice grown primarily in the summer.
 
• The cultivation period is relatively short, typically around 90-100 days.
 
• It is usually rain-fed and requires less water compared to other types.
 
 
 
• **Aman**
 
 
• Aman rice is a major rice crop grown during the monsoon season.
 
• It requires a longer growing period, usually around 150-180 days.
 
• This variety is highly dependent on adequate monsoon rainfall.
 
 
 
• **Boro**
 
 
• Boro rice is cultivated in the winter season and harvested in the spring.
 
• It is grown in areas with assured irrigation as it needs a lot of water.
 
• Boro rice typically has a high yield and is an important crop for food security in West Bengal.
